items.name: Optomize
items.tagline: Optometry EMR suite — markdown case files, ∆-delta follow-up visits and cross-patient pattern matching that stores only what changed.
items.description: Optomize turns the sidebar into an optometry EMR composer. Type an MR number and the chart inherits the patient's last visit automatically — you only store the difference (∆iop:OD=16, ∆va:OS=6/9) while everything else resolves from the prior record at read time. When a new patient matches an existing one, the matcher finds the best matched pair and writes pattern=MR plus just the real differences (∆H/O -DM). Every visit lands in the clinic folder frontmatter so it shows up in Bases, and a Clinic EMR database view is seeded on first save.
items.author: FocusCaseX originals

items.name: Focuslinks Navigation
items.tagline: Turns the left sidebar into pure clinical navigation — a grouped Clinic navigator (Front desk · Clinical · Insights across 7 seeded pages) replaces the Files/Bases/EMR clutter. Each page docks its own right-panel tools.
items.description: Focuslinks Navigation owns the left sidebar only — and only navigation lives there. It hides the raw Files tree, Database bases and the Optomize composer, and puts a grouped clinical navigator in their place: FRONT DESK (Appointments, Recalls, Billing), CLINICAL (Patient List, Prescriptions) and INSIGHTS (Reports, Cohorts) — each seeded on first enable and rendered as a full clinical UI in the center panel: ui-appointment (the interactive appointment book with day/week/month calendar tabs and booking), ui-recalls (the overdue follow-up safety board), ui-flow (appointment→checkout workflow tracker with per-stage patient lists and one-tap stage advance), ui-patients (the live patient directory) and ui-billing (the front desk's to-bill / dispensing / unbilled worklist). The front desk itself — the composite appointment-board + funnel + cash-desk landing — lives at Database/Dashboard and needs no navigator entry. Exams open from patient flows (booking rows, patient rows), never a menu. Every page can write its own right panel inline with a ui-panel block — a booking form, the day's pipeline, today's pulse or quick actions dock in the right context panel exactly as the page declares. The navigator stays lean — grouped page links and nothing else. UI pages stay out of the Files tree unless Developer mode is on. Editing the UI source stays locked until Developer mode is enabled in Settings — where a dedicated Developer tab lists every UI page and every block with its spec. Ships its own CSS (managed like a snippet, removed on disable) that orders the sections and styles the reading view's tables as appointment boards with status pills.
items.author: FocusCaseX originals

items.name: Essential Diagrams
items.tagline: Clinical-atlas eye diagrams for the Examination workup — tap-to-select anterior segment (surface, cornea & iris, lacrimal drainage) and fundus (posterior pole, periphery) views for OD and OS, label each finding, and add the labeled results straight into the exam note.
items.description: Essential Diagrams is the Examination workup's eye-diagram engine — it never surfaces as app chrome. The exam embeds it as a clinical sheet with flat ATLAS-STYLE diagrams: an ANTERIOR SEGMENT view (surface & adnexa, cornea/iris/pupil detail, and the full lacrimal drainage system — puncta, canaliculi, common canaliculus, lacrimal sac and nasolacrimal duct) and a FUNDUS view (posterior pole — disc, neuroretinal rim, cup, macula, fovea, vascular arcades and vessels — plus a flattened retinal-periphery chart with the four quadrant zones). Every structure is its own tap-to-select region, tracked independently for OD and OS with a one-tap eye switch and a mirrored OS presentation. Each selected structure takes a free-text LABEL ("cornea — 2×3 mm paracentral scar"), and one tap adds the labeled findings into the workup's Slit-lamp findings / Fundus findings fields. A "Remember selections" settings pane completes the surface.
items.author: FocusCaseX originals

items.name: UtilityPannel
items.tagline: Adopts the right panel each page writes for itself — a ```ui-panel block inside any clinical page docks its booking form, pipeline, pulse or actions in the right context panel exactly as declared.
items.description: UtilityPannel owns the right context panel — and nothing else. It adds no tools and no pages of its own: when a clinical page carries a ```ui-panel block, UtilityPannel adopts that block and docks exactly what the page wrote (a booking form, the day's pipeline, today's pulse, quick action buttons) into the right panel while the page is open. No fence, no panel — the adaptive patient/book/pulse context takes back over. The panel's code always stays in the page that wrote it: with Developer mode on, a Panel elements dock appears at the foot of that page where every value and element line of the block is visible and editable in place, so the panel stays customizable without end.
